§ 2Content

§ 3Motion

  • A relative change in the position of an object with respect to a reference point is called motion.
  • Opposite of Motion: Rest (when the body is still and not moving).
  • Motion is mainly described in terms of the following terms:
  • Distance: It refers to the total length of the path an object travels, regardless of direction and is a scalar quantity.
  • Displacement: It is the shortest path between the initial and final positions (not the total distance) and is a vector quantity.

#### Case 1

A person walks directly from point A to point B.

  • Distance covered = 50 m.
  • Displacement = 50 m.
  • The person walks in a straight line.

#### Case 2

A person walks directly from point A to point B and returns back to point A.

  • Distance covered = 100 m (50 m to B + 50 m back to A).
  • Displacement = 0 m.
  • The displacement is only from initial to final position.
Scalar QuantityVector Quantity
It only represents numerical value (magnitude)It represents both numerical value (magnitude) and direction
E.g. Distance, Speed, TimeE.g. Displacement, Velocity

Point to Remember

  • km/hr × 5/18 = m/s
  • m/s × 18/5 = km/hr

International system of units (S.I.) was established in 1960.

  • Speed: It is the rate at which an object's position changes with time, regardless of the direction of motion. Its S.I. unit is meters per second (m/s) and is a scalar quantity.

Average Speed

  • The average speed is the ratio of total distance traveled by the object to the total time taken to cover that distance. It is a scalar quantity.

Average Speed = Total Distance Covered / Total Time Taken

Questionnaire

An object travels 16 m in 4 sec and then another 16 m in 2 sec. What is the average speed of the object?

Sol:

Average Speed = Total Distance Covered / Total Time Taken

= (16 + 16) / (4 + 2) = 32/6 = 5.33 m/s

Types of Motion

  • There are two types of motion: Uniform and Non-Uniform motion.
  1. 1. Uniform Motion: Uniform motion is characterized by an object moving in a straight line with a constant velocity, which means that it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, resulting in zero acceleration. E.g. If the speed of a car is 10 m/s, it means that the car covers 10 meters in one second. The speed is constant every second.
  • Linear (Rectilinear) Motion: An object moving in a straight line at a constant speed (constant velocity).
  • Circular Motion: An object moving along a circular path at a constant speed (constant angular velocity).
  • Rotational Motion: An object rotating around a fixed axis at a constant angular speed.
  1. 2. Non-Uniform Motion: Non-uniform motion is when an object's speed or direction changes over time, so it doesn't cover equal distances in equal time intervals. E.g. If a car covers 10 meters in the first two seconds and 15 meters in the next two seconds.
  • Linear (Rectilinear) Motion: An object moving in a straight line with changing speed (acceleration).
  • Circular Motion: An object moving along a circular path with changing speed (acceleration).
  • Rotational Motion: An object rotating around a fixed axis with changing angular speed (angular acceleration).

§ 4Motion (continued)

Types of motion illustrations: Vibratory Motion, Linear Motion, Curvilinear Motion, Oscillatory Motion, Circular Motion, Rotary Motion.

Velocity

  • Velocity is the rate at which an object changes its position in a specific direction. Unlike speed, velocity is a vector quantity, which means it has both magnitude and direction. The S.I. unit of velocity is m/s.

Speed + Direction = Velocity

Velocity = Displacement / Time

v = d/t, t = d/v, d = v × t

Odometer: It is used to measure the distance travelled by a vehicle.

Questionnaire

Usha swims in a 90 m long pool. She covers 180 m in one minute by swimming from one end to the other and back along the same straight path. The average speed and average velocity of Usha respectively is?

→ Since, she covers 180 m in one minute by swimming from one end to the other and back along the same straight path, therefore, displacement of Usha in 1 min = 0 m.

Average Speed = 180 m / (1 × 60 s) = 3 m/s

Average Velocity = 0 / (1 × 60 s) = 0 m/s

Acceleration

  • Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. It essentially describes how quickly an object's speed or direction (or both) is changing. The S.I. unit of acceleration is m/s².

Acceleration = a_c

a_c = Change in Velocity / Time (Δt)

= (Final Velocity − Initial Velocity) / Time (Δt)

= (v − u) / Δt

Questionnaire

Starting from a stationary position, Rahul paddles his bicycle to attain a velocity of 6 m/s in 30 s. Then he applies brakes such that the velocity of bicycle comes down to 4 m/s in the next 5 s. Calculate the acceleration of the bicycle in both the cases.

Sol:

Case 1: He starts from a stationary position and attains speed of 6 m/s in 30 s.

  • Initial velocity (u) = 0 m/s
  • Final velocity (v) = 6 m/s
  • Time taken (Δt) = 30 s
  • a_c = (6 − 0) / 30 = 6/30 = 1/5 = 0.2 m/s²

Case 2: He applies brakes such that the velocity of the bicycle comes down to 4 m/s in next 5 s. Final velocity in Case 1 becomes the initial velocity in Case 2.

  • Initial velocity (u) = 6 m/s
  • Final velocity (v) = 4 m/s
  • Time taken (Δt) = 5 s
  • a_c = (4 − 6) / 5 = −2/5 = −0.4 m/s²

Graph Representation

A distance-time graph shows how far an object has travelled over a period of time. Distance is plotted on the Y-axis and time is plotted on the X-axis.

What it tells us:

  • The slope of the graph gives the speed of the object.
  • A straight line with a constant slope means the object is moving at a constant speed.
  • A curved line indicates that the speed is changing, which may mean acceleration or deceleration.

Displacement-Time Graph

  • For Stationary Body (Body at rest): Horizontal line
  • For Uniform Motion: Straight line with constant slope
  • For Non-Uniform Motion (speed increases): Curved line

§ 5Motion (continued)

Numerical of Motion in a straight line: The "UTSAV" Concept

  • In case of uniform acceleration, there are three equations of motion that describe the motion of an object with constant acceleration.
  1. 1. v = u + at
  2. 2. s = ut + ½ at²
  3. 3. v² − u² = 2as
  • u: Initial velocity
  • t: Time
  • s: Distance
  • a: Acceleration
  • v: Final velocity

When an object starts from a stationary position or starts to free fall, its initial velocity (u) is 0 m/s.

Deceleration, also known as negative acceleration or retardation, refers to a decrease in an object's speed or velocity, which is the opposite of acceleration (increasing speed or velocity).

Motion Under Gravity

  • Motion under gravity (also known as free-fall motion) refers to the movement of an object solely influenced by the force of gravity, resulting in a constant downward acceleration (approximately 9.8 m/s²).
  1. 1. v = u + gt
  2. 2. s = ut + ½ gt²
  3. 3. v² − u² = 2gh

a = g → Acceleration due to gravity

Free fall → u = 0 (initial speed)

Upward Motion (against the gravity)

  1. 1. v = u − gt
  2. 2. s = ut − ½ gt²
  3. 3. v² − u² = −2gh

a = −g, final velocity at highest point = 0

Questionnaire

A train starting from rest attains a velocity of 72 km/h in 5 minutes. Assuming that the acceleration is uniform. The distance travelled by train for the above velocity is?

Sol:

Initial velocity (u) = 0 km/h, Final velocity (v) = 72 km/h = 20 m/s and Time (t) = 5 min.

As per the first law of motion

v = u + at

20 = 0 + (a_c × 5 × 60)

a_c = 20 / (5 × 60) = 1/15 m/s²

Distance travelled by train

S = ut + ½ at²

S = 0 × 300 + ½ × (1/15) × 300² = 3000 m = 3 km

Uniform Circular Motion

  • The motion of a body moving with a constant speed along a circular path is called Uniform Circular Motion.

a_c = v²/r

a_c: Centripetal acceleration (acceleration towards the centre in circular path)

Centripetal force is the force acting on a body in a circular path. It points towards the center around which the body is moving.

  • For a body moving in uniform circular motion the speed attained by the object will remain constant not the velocity as velocity depends on the direction of motion, and in circular motion the direction of the object changes at every point. This continuous change in velocity results in an acceleration, even though the speed is constant.

Questionnaire

An athlete completes one round of a circular track of diameter 100 m in 20 s. What will be the displacement after 1 min and 10 s, respectively?

Sol:

  • Diameter of the track = 100 m
  • One complete round takes, t = 20 s
  • Total Time = 1 min and 10 s = 70 s
  • No. of rounds = 70/20 = 3.5 rounds

After 3 full rounds, the athlete comes back to the starting point, so displacement = 0.

After 0.5 round, the athlete reaches the diametrically opposite point of the circle.

Displacement after 3.5 rounds = Diameter of the circle

Displacement = 100 m

('because as you know, displacement is the shortest distance between the initial and final point).
